summary: BLOCKING RELEASE PREREQUISITE, raised from Wave 33 and still unactioned; this lane made it worse in a way release must know about. Three server-side fan-outs now refuse to make any outbound request unless an operator has declared an internal origin, because deriving the destination from the inbound request was the SSRF defect (CodeQL alert #16 and the two unflagged siblings at app/api/hub/route.ts and lib/news/feed-service.ts, all now fixed). The guard has NO fallback and NO localhost default, so an environment with none of these variables set does not error — it silently returns empty sections. Affected surfaces, all in discover's charter: GET /api/discover (whole aggregation fan-out: posts, events, music, suggestions, people, albums, tours), GET /api/hub (discover + news + jobs sections), and the news feed's external RSS candidates (GET /api/news/feed and GET /api/feed/for-you lose their external items). The variables read, in precedence order, are INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN, then NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, then VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL, then VERCEL_URL. All four are read server-side from process.env; they may be space- or comma-separated lists; a source whose value contains any unusable entry contributes nothing at all, so a typo yields an empty allowlist rather than a widened one. DISCOVER_ALLOW_LOCAL_UPSTREAM is a development-only opt-in and must be left UNSET in every deployed environment: a loopback or private-literal origin is refused outright when NODE_ENV=production even with it set.

completed: Named the exact variable set and its precedence order in the guard's own documentation, in DECISIONS.md, in the discover domain decision log, and in the discover STATE.md, so it is not a tribal memory item.

Made each affected route log a distinct, actionable warning naming the variable to set, so the failure is diagnosable from logs instead of being a silent empty response. Before this the news surface had no signal at all.
Recorded the prerequisite as a named blocking item on DISC-002 acceptance and in its blockers, not only in a handoff.
Confirmed the guard fails CLOSED and never widens: no allowlisted origin means zero outbound requests, and a partially-parseable env value means zero allowlisted origins, not a subset.
next_steps: Set INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN explicitly in every deployed environment (production, staging, preview) to the app's own absolute https origin. Prefer it over relying on the Vercel-provided variables, because VERCEL_URL is a per-deployment value and the preview origin changes on every deploy.
Leave DISCOVER_ALLOW_LOCAL_UPSTREAM unset in every deployed environment. It is only for local development against http://127.0.0.1:3000 and is ignored when NODE_ENV=production.

If a base path or a non-default port is ever needed, note that the guard rejects a configured origin that carries a path, query, or fragment, so INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN must be a bare scheme://host[:port].

Smoke each of the three surfaces after the variable is set and confirm non-empty sections: /api/discover returns sections.for_you and stats.trending_count above zero, /api/hub returns metrics.headlines above zero, and /api/news/feed returns at least one originType 'external' item. An empty result with the warning absent means the origin resolves but the upstream rejects; an empty result WITH the warning means the allowlist is still empty.
Grep the deploy configuration for the four variable names before promoting, and record which environment each was set in, so a later wave does not have to re-derive it.
blockers: Until this is set, /api/discover returns empty sections, /api/hub returns zeroed metrics, and the news feed has no external RSS candidates — by design, not by bug. Treat it as blocking for the launch graph, because DISC-002 is a P1 launch dependency.
